3.author: St. John Chrysostom
3.work: Homilies on the Gospel of St. Matthew, Homily 15
3.text: Chrysostom reads 'poor in spirit' as the cure for the disease the Sermon on the Mount is preached against. The world calls poverty a misfortune; Christ calls a certain poverty the door of the Kingdom. To be poor in spirit, Chrysostom says, is to think humbly of oneself, to consider oneself as nothing, to feel the lowliness of one's condition before God. It is not the bowed shoulders of the beggar but the bowed mind of every Christian who knows he stands by grace and not by right.

3.author: St. Gregory of Nyssa
3.text: Gregory of Nyssa makes 'poverty of spirit' the gateway to every other beatitude. Christ Himself, he says, became poor that we might be made rich; the Christian who follows Him learns the same descent. Earthly poverty without poverty of spirit gains nothing; poverty of spirit without earthly possessions can still own everything in the love of God. The blessedness is in the disposition, not in the bank account.
